chunks: A number of our companions, from Saahl ibn Ziyaad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from 'Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a guest from his brothers with him, and the Day of Fitrah arrives; does he pay the Fitrah on his behalf? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. The Fitrah is obligatory upon everyone who has dependents, from male or female, young or old, free or slave.'

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr), the obligatory charity paid at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Is a man required to pay Fitrah for a guest staying with him on Eid al-Fitr?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the host bears the obligation of Fitrah for a guest from his brothers, as the guest is considered a dependent (ma'ool) under the host's care. This ruling underscores the principle that Zakat al-Fitr is tied to one's financial responsibility for others, ensuring that all dependents, regardless of age or status, are covered during the festive occasion. The hadith highlights the communal nature of purification and charity in Shia jurisprudence, where the head of the household ensures the spiritual cleanliness of those under his provision.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Saheyl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happens to have the guest from his brethren with him. So the day of the Fitra presents itself. Does he have to pay the Fitra on his behalf?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. The Fitra is Obligatory upon everyone who has dependents, from the male, or female, or young, or old, be they free or slaves’.
en.sarwar: 16. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who has a guest from his brothers and the day of al-Fitrah comes; if he must pay al-Fitrah for him. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, al-Fitrah is obligatory for everyone whom you count of your dependents, male, female, children, grown up, free or slaves.’”
